newsitem.title: USA: Aquila taps Diana Herrmann for president's post.
newsitem.headline: Aquila taps Diana Herrmann for president's post.

text.p: Aquila Management Corp's Diana Herrmann will succeed her father as president of the New York-based company which sponsors seven single-state municipal bond funds.
While Diana, 39, has been named president and chief operating officer. Her father, Aquila founder Lacy Herrmann, will remain chairman and chief executive officer of the firm, an Aquila release said.

"I am pleased to turn the day-to-day operation of the firm over to Diana," the elder Herrmann said in the release. "She has thoroughly proven herself and is fully knowledgeable about our business and the fund industry."

Diana Herrmann has been with Aquila since 1986, serving most recently as executive vice president. Aquila sponsors 14 mutual funds with nearly $3 billion in assets. She is a board member of seven funds, and an officer on all 14.

"This change enables me to focus my efforts more heavily on further development of our company, especially in the creation of new products and general oversight of policies and strategies," her father said.

Aquila's seven single-state municipal bond funds are in smaller population states with high tax rates. The seven are: Churchill Tax-Free Fund of Kentucky, Hawaiian Tax-Free Trust, Narragansett Insured Tax-Free Income Fund, Tax-Free Fund for Utah, Tax-Free Fund of Colorado, Tax-Free Trust of Arizona, and Tax-Free Trust of Oregon.
The company also has two regional stock funds and five money market funds.
Before joining Aquila, Diana Herrmann worked at European American Bank in New York, and was a board member and secretary of the Bank Credit Association.

She is active in the mutual fund industry, serving on several Investment Company Institute committees. A graduate of the Advanced Management Program: The International Senior Managers' Program at Harvard Business School, she is an alumna of Colby College.
